jp_verse: 木の床に　一つの柿が光り\n\n    障子の午後が　静けさを包む
en_verse: A single persimmon glowed upon the wooden floor,\nwhile afternoon light through the shoji held the room in stillness.

jp_verse: 夜の寺に　二つの灯が浮かび\n\n    やわらかな闇だけが　揺れていた
en_verse: Two lanterns drifted above the temple at night,\nwhile only the gentle darkness swayed.

jp_verse: 黒い台に　三つの柿が並び\n\n    扇のそばで　秋が息づいていた
en_verse: Three persimmons rested upon the dark tray,\nand beside the folded fan, autumn quietly breathed.

jp_verse: 四つの柿が　盆の上に並び\n\n    障子の影が　秋の部屋を包む
en_verse: Four persimmons lined up upon the tray,\nwhile maple shadows on the shoji wrapped the autumn room.

jp_verse: 五つの鯉のぼりが　風に泳ぎ\n\n    川の上だけが　春を映していた
en_verse: Five carp streamed in the wind above the river,\nwhile only the water mirrored the spring.

jp_verse: 六つの茶碗に　湯気が立ち\n\n    静かな席が　人を待っていた
en_verse: Steam rose from six tea bowls in a row,\nwhile the quiet seats waited for their guests.

jp_verse: 七匹の鯉が　池を泳ぎ\n\n    一匹だけが　月へ向かっていた
en_verse: Seven koi glided through the moonlit pond,\nwhile one alone turned toward the moon.

jp_verse: 巨木の根で　道が二つに裂け\n\n    旅人だけが　選択を止めていた
en_verse: At the roots of the great tree the path split in two,\nand the traveler alone paused before the choice.

jp_verse: 濡れた橋に\n\n    灯りが続く
en_verse: Lights continuing across the wet bridge.

jp_verse: 朝の市で　藍の布を畳み\n\n    十の交わりが　布に静かに刻まれた
en_verse: At the morning market he folded indigo cloth,\nand the crossing of ten lay quietly woven in the fabric.

jp_verse: 湯気の立つ碗を　両手で包み\n\n    口を開けて　笑いが部屋に溢れた
en_verse: Holding the steaming bowl in both hands,\nshe opened her mouth and laughter filled the room.

jp_verse: 棚田に　朝日が降り注ぎ\n\n    水面だけが　黄金に燃えていた
en_verse: Morning sun poured across the terraced fields,\nwhile only the water burned with gold.

jp_verse: 船上で網を直す漁師に\n\n    月明かりだけが　静かに寄り添った
en_verse: A fisherman mended his net upon the boat,\nwhile moonlight alone quietly kept him company.

jp_verse: 方眼の田が　朝日を映し\n\n    霧の谷だけが　静かに包んでいた
en_verse: The grid of paddies mirrored the morning sun,\nwhile only the misty valley quietly held them.

jp_verse: 橋の上で　灯りの流れを見つめ\n\n    少年の目だけが　夜を覚えていた
en_verse: Upon the bridge he watched the lanterns drift,\nwhile only the boy's eyes remembered the night.

jp_verse:
古い杉の幹に

    朝の光が差し

    幾世代もの祈りを

    静かに宿していた
en_verse:
Morning light touched
the trunk of the ancient cedar,
which quietly carried
the prayers of generations.

jp_verse: 鏡の前に　静かに立ち\n\n    言葉なくして　我だけが在った
en_verse: He stood quietly before the mirror,\nand without words, only himself remained.

jp_verse: 雪の嶺で　伸ばした手を握り\n\n    見えぬ一歩が　二人を結んでいた
en_verse: Upon the snowy ridge they clasped reaching hands,\nand one unseen step bound them together.

jp_verse: 雪の庭を　向かい合いながら\n\n    火鉢のぬくもりだけが　二人をつないでいた
en_verse: Facing each other across the snowy garden,\nonly the warmth of the brazier joined them together.

jp_verse: 炉の火が　二人の顔を照らし\n\n    明るい笑いだけが　部屋に残った
en_verse: The hearth fire lit their faces with warmth,\nand only their bright laughter lingered in the room.
